mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES continues to rise from its current level while TRANSIT remains deeply negative, weekday foot traffic should still recover through commuting-linked errands and lunch trips, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES has improved from -23.3 to -18.4 while RETAIL_REC weakened to -17.7
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stays below its prior 4-week mean even as WORKPLACES rises for two more consecutive weeks and TRANSIT does not fall further.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in PARKS mobility after a previously elevated level signals substitution back toward indoor discretionary trips; when PARKS falls below about 15 points, retail visits should improve within one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below 15 points after being above 25 points in the prior two weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from 35.0 at t-3w to 12.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week after PARKS crosses below 15 points, or continues falling despite the drop in PARKS.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT declines further while RESIDENTIAL rises, it indicates tighter movement constraints that suppress shopping trips; under that tightening regime, RETAIL_REC should fall relative to the previous four weeks over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT drops below -25 points and RESIDENTIAL exceeds +5 points in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT moved from -22.9 to -24.0 while RESIDENTIAL rose from 2.9 to 5.1
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is not lower than its last-4-week mean after the TRANSIT/RESIDENTIAL threshold is met for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A continued easing in GROCERY_PHARM mobility toward normal levels frees household time from necessity shopping and supports discretionary retail visits, so RETAIL_REC should increase over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved from -9.6 to -7.4 while RETAIL_REC deteriorated to -17.7
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains flat or declines over the next 14 days despite further movement of GROCERY_PHARM toward zero.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility keeps rising and WORKPLACES keep recovering, people substitute local convenience purchasing for large shopping trips; that combination should keep RETAIL_REC below the prior month's average over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose from 2.9 to 5.1 while WORKPLACES improved from -23.3 to -18.4
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-week mean while RESIDENTIAL stays above 5 and WORKPLACES continues improving.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rebound in PARKS after its recent plunge should precede warmer-weather discretionary activity shifts and pull shoppers away from indoor retail, lowering RETAIL_REC within four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rebounds by at least 10 points from its recent low
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS dropped from 35.0 to 11.3 before a small rebound to 12.9
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not weaken after PARKS recovers by 10 points or more from the recent trough.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT stops falling and instead recovers above its current trough, the policy effect of mobility easing should transmit quickly to shopping corridors, producing higher RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises at least 3 points from the current weekly mean
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT is still near -24.0 after four weeks around -22 to -24
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve in the next week after TRANSIT rebounds by at least 3 points.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous recovery in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT indicates more commuting and city-center circulation; that interaction should lift retail-and-recreation demand over the next two to four weeks unless PARKS also surges and diverts discretionary outings.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both rise week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved while TRANSIT remained deeply negative
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise within 2 weeks even though WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both increase together, or PARKS rises enough to offset the commuting effect.
